hook: You may need fewer fans than you think

insight.title: 1,000 True Fans
paras: Kevin Kelly’s 1,000 True Fans is a creator-economics heuristic, not a promise. The simple idea: a smaller group that keeps buying and sharing can matter more than a huge group that only scrolls past.

Here is one example. You want to earn $100,000. Each loyal supporter brings $100 in profit over the year. 1,000 people × $100 = $100,000. That is why the example says 1,000 fans. Your real number may be different.

insight.visualCaption: One thousand supporters times one hundred dollars each reaches a one-hundred-thousand-dollar goal.
after: For Daily Insight, do not only count views. Count who comes back, finishes a lesson, saves it, replies, or shares it.

For a paid project, start with one goal and one honest estimate of the profit from each loyal customer. The point is to see whether you need millions of strangers—or a smaller group you serve very well.

lab.title: Try It With Ten People
paras: Use tiny numbers first so the idea is easy to see.
lab.exercise: Imagine a $1,000 goal. If ten loyal people each bring $100 in profit, you reach it: 10 × $100 = $1,000. Now swap in one real goal from your work. Keep only one example on the page.

storyVideoPlan.style: Warm editorial storybook animation with hand-painted gouache and risograph texture, bold cobalt, amber, coral and teal shapes, one recurring adult protagonist named Maya, no photorealism, no logos, no spoken characters
storyVideoPlan.narration: Maya has fifty thousand followers, but her studio struggles to pay bills. Most people tap like and move on. They never buy. They never come back. The big number does not keep her studio open. A smaller group acts differently. They return, buy a workshop, tell a friend, and support Maya again. That loyal group, not the giant crowd, is the engine. This idea is called One Thousand True Fans. It is a rule of thumb, not magic. Here is the simple math. Maya wants to earn one hundred thousand dollars this year. If each loyal supporter brings one hundred dollars in profit, then one thousand supporters bring one hundred thousand dollars. One thousand people, times one hundred dollars each, equals her goal. That is all the math means. Your number may be different. For Daily Insight, forget follower count. Watch who returns, finishes a lesson, saves it, replies, or shares it. Build for those people. Depth first. Reach second.

blocks.narration: Maya has fifty thousand followers, but her studio struggles to pay the bills. Most people scroll past her work and never come back.
blocks.prompt: Vertical 9:16 warm editorial storybook animation matching the supplied Maya reference exactly: adult woman with short dark curly bob, teal sweater, ochre trousers, cobalt-amber-coral-teal gouache and risograph texture. Exactly five hard-cut shots, about two seconds each, with motion from frame one. Shot 1 WIDE: Maya works at a warm creative studio desk while a huge cloud of tiny follower dots swirls above her phone. Shot 2 HIGH ANGLE: unpaid bills slide across the desk as the follower cloud keeps growing. Shot 3 CLOSE-UP: the phone counter races upward while Maya's worried eyes reflect it. Shot 4 LOW ANGLE: the enormous counter shadow overwhelms the small studio. Shot 5 MEDIUM: Maya lowers the phone and looks toward a small glowing circle offscreen. Characters emote and gesture but never talk; no lip sync, no readable text, no logos.

blocks.narration: A smaller group returns, buys a workshop, tells a friend, and supports her again. That loyal group, not the giant crowd, is the engine.
blocks.prompt: Vertical 9:16 continuation in the identical warm gouache-risograph editorial storybook world and identical Maya character. Exactly five hard-cut shots, about two seconds each, all moving from frame one. Shot 1 MEDIUM: a small circle of diverse adult supporters enters Maya's studio carrying sketchbooks. Shot 2 CLOSE-UP: hands exchange workshop tickets and handmade prints. Shot 3 OVERHEAD: the same supporters return around a round table month after month as calendar pages flip. Shot 4 SIDE ANGLE: one supporter enthusiastically brings a friend into the circle. Shot 5 WIDE: the small circle glows brightly while the distant follower cloud fades. Characters gesture but never talk; no lip sync, no readable text, no logos.

blocks.narration: This idea is called One Thousand True Fans. It is not magic or a promise. It asks how many loyal supporters you actually need.
blocks.prompt: Vertical 9:16 continuation in the identical warm gouache-risograph editorial storybook style. Exactly five hard-cut shots, about two seconds each, immediate motion. Shot 1 MACRO: one glowing supporter token pulses in Maya's hand. Shot 2 TOP-DOWN: many warm tokens ripple outward into an organized ring. Shot 3 WIDE: the ring resolves into a symbolic crowd of one thousand lights around Maya's studio. Shot 4 HIGH ANGLE: a glittering magic-wand shortcut appears, cracks, and dissolves to show this is not magic. Shot 5 MEDIUM: Maya calmly weighs the glowing supporter ring against a faded viral rocket symbol. Characters gesture but never talk; no lip sync, no readable text, no logos.

blocks.narration: Maya wants to earn one hundred thousand dollars this year. If each supporter brings one hundred dollars in profit, she needs one thousand supporters.
blocks.prompt: Vertical 9:16 continuation in the identical warm editorial storybook animation. Exactly five hard-cut shots, about two seconds each, motion from frame one. Shot 1 OVERHEAD: Maya places a large gold income token above a hand-drawn division line. Shot 2 MACRO: a coral supporter-value token slides beneath the line. Shot 3 SIDE ANGLE: the tokens click into a simple mechanical calculator. Shot 4 CLOSE-UP: the machine releases ten neat bundles of one hundred glowing supporter lights. Shot 5 WIDE: one thousand lights form a stable warm bridge supporting Maya's studio. Characters gesture but never talk; no lip sync, no readable text or numerals, no logos.

blocks.narration: One hundred dollars from each of one thousand people adds up to one hundred thousand dollars. If each person brings less, she needs more.
blocks.prompt: Vertical 9:16 continuation in the identical warm gouache-risograph storybook world. Exactly five hard-cut shots, about two seconds each, immediate motion. Shot 1 CLOSE-UP: the coral value token visibly shrinks in Maya's palm. Shot 2 LOW ANGLE: the calculator gears spin much faster. Shot 3 WIDE: the supporter-light bridge stretches five times farther across the studio. Shot 4 TOP-DOWN: four tactile levers for value, margin, return visits, and direct connection slide to different positions. Shot 5 MEDIUM: Maya adjusts one lever and watches the required crowd expand and contract. Characters gesture but never talk; no lip sync, no readable text, no logos.

blocks.narration: For Daily Insight, count who returns, finishes a lesson, saves it, replies, or shares it. Build for those people. Depth first. Reach second.
blocks.prompt: Vertical 9:16 finale in the identical warm editorial storybook animation and identical Maya character. Exactly five hard-cut shots, about two seconds each, moving immediately. Shot 1 CLOSE-UP: Maya swipes through a Daily Insight-like lesson on a generic phone with illustrated cards and no readable interface text. Shot 2 OVERHEAD: learner tokens return, finish a path, save a card, reply, and invite another token through clear pictograms. Shot 3 MEDIUM: those actions feed a warm circular flywheel around the phone. Shot 4 WIDE: the flywheel strengthens a small deep-rooted tree while a giant shallow follower cloud blows away. Shot 5 CLOSE-UP: Maya smiles, pockets the phone, and the rooted learning circle glows behind her. Characters gesture but never talk; no lip sync, no readable text, no logos.

steal.line: Build for depth before you buy reach.
paras: Use this whenever a growth discussion jumps straight to follower counts. It redirects the conversation toward value per person and the behaviors that reveal durable demand.
example: In a Daily Insight review: “Before we chase more reach, which signal proves the people already here are returning, finishing, saving, replying, or referring?”
